A spear.

Easy to learn (but difficult to master). Keep people at a distance where they can't hit you. Easy to fix if it breaks. Cheap to make.

The spear is arguably the most popular melee weapon ever, and with good reason. It's basically just a pointy stick.

To add to the spear arugment, the big thing a spear has that makes it so effective is range and versatility. Pole arms in general are just better for reach and make for an all around easier to handle weapons than say a sword, regardless of origin. A lot of people say "well as soon as they grab the stick end you're screwed" but this is to assume that you are one unaware of this and two just wielding it wildly. Any one who is going to use a weapon should be trying to learn some technique with it. I have no proper training with any weapon, so if you were to just give me a spear vs. a sword, the spear is easier to grasp and understand, poke them and keep away, while a sword requires understanding edge alignment, heavy upkeep, and putting yourself in a more dangerous position to make effective. But then, if I had a spear, I would be training with it constantly if I was wanting to learn how to use it propperly as a weapon, as one should with any weapon regardless of what it is. But just because a spear has draw backs or is easier to pick up does not make it "scrub mode" (to which if you believe that in a survival situation you are not going to live long to begin with). A spear is easy to manufacture and make multiple of, so losing one is not necessarily a problem. Spears can be thrown as well as grasped to keep opponents at bay. In tight quarters a spear can actually be very useful for keeping back opponents since you just have to point the sharp end in the direction of your opponent, making it harder to reach you, which is the important part of understanding what makes a spear so good. Having a spear means your opponent has a harder time getting to you. And if you're really worried about people getting past the pointy bit, keep a handax or dagger on hand as a side arm. But for me I'd probably just have a gun. And at that point well I have a gun.

But the final point to why the spear is the best is the simple fact that of any weapon it is the easiest to pick up and still use to a degree better than say a sword. And again if I were in a situation where I found myself suddenly in possession of a spear and had to fight for survival, the day I picked it up I would be practicing how to make myself better with it. The biggest thing to remember with any martial art is that it all comes down to taste. A sword is just as effective as a spear. But it isn't easier to learn, which doesn't necessarily make it better.

A knife, spear, or other penetrating weapon requires that you first of all are dealing with an unarmored opponent, and that you are able to make a strong enough blow to stop their assault. Attackers who are dressed head-to-toe in armor are unlikely in any scenario except the martial law one. Even then, a stun baton is an enormously powerful weapon, about the only answer to a stun baton is a gun.

Even when set to stun, in their incapacitated state your victim is completely vulnerable, and you will be free to dispatch them using their own weapon.
